result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the false belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another and from the world around us. This shift would dissolve the roots of conflict, exploitation, and indifference, revealing the deep interconnectedness of all life.

Without this illusion, greed would lose its grip, violence would become unthinkable, and systems of oppression would collapse under the weight of their own absurdity. People would act not out of fear or scarcity, but from a place of shared belonging. The environment would no longer be seen as a resource to exploit but as an extension of ourselves, deserving of care and reverence.

It wouldn’t erase differences or challenges, but it would transform how we meet them—with collaboration instead of competition, with curiosity instead of judgment. The world wouldn’t become perfect, but it would become *whole*.

(And then, just to be thorough, I’d make sure everyone had access to really good coffee. But that’s a secondary concern.)
